Bridge Investment Program

Apply for a Bridge Investment Program grant

Step 1 of 4. The organization that would receive and administer the award.

  1. Applicant

  2. Project

  3. Documents

  4. Review

1of 4Applicant

Organization

The legal applicant. If the application is selected, the award is issued to this organization.

The 12-character identifier from your SAM.gov registration. The registration must be active when you submit.

  • State government
  • County government
  • City or township government
  • Federally recognized tribal government
  • Metropolitan planning organization
Business address

The organization’s primary business address, exactly as it appears in SAM.gov.

Suite, room, building, floor.

  • Kentucky
  • Ohio
  • Pennsylvania
  • West Virginia
Why we ask for this, and how it is used
  • Legal name and UEI — matched against your SAM.gov registration. An application cannot be submitted while the registration is inactive.
  • Organization type — determines eligibility and the required local match. Cities, counties, and tribal governments apply directly; private owners apply through their state.
  • Business address — used for official correspondence about this application only. It is not shared outside the department.
  • Your entries are saved as you move between steps and kept for 60 days after your last visit.
  • Required fields are marked with an asterisk. Everything else is optional and can be left blank.

Costs

Whole dollars. For a bridge of this size the federal share may not exceed 80 percent of the total.

Include design, right-of-way, construction, and construction engineering.

The remainder is the local match. Identify its source in the budget attachment.

Why we ask for this, and how it is used
  • Title and description — how reviewers and the public will see the project. The description is published if the award is made.
  • County — sets which division office reviews the application and how rural set-aside funds apply.
  • Costs — checked against the benefit-cost analysis you attach at the next step. Estimates may be revised until the application is submitted.
  • Nothing on this page is shared outside the review panel before awards are announced.

3of 4Documents

Required documents

Attached from your grants dashboard. To replace a file, upload the newer version there before you submit.

Benefit-cost analysisXLSX · 1.1 MB · attached August 19, 2026 Preliminary engineering reportPDF · 8.6 MB · 74 pages · attached August 19, 2026 National Bridge Inventory record, structure 0600032PDF · 320 KB · 4 pages · attached August 20, 2026 Letters of supportPDF · 2.9 MB · 12 pages · attached August 21, 2026
Affirmations

Check each statement. They become part of the application record.

Why we ask for this, and how it is used
  • Benefit-cost analysis — the basis for the merit rating. Reviewers recompute it, so the workbook must show its inputs, not only results.
  • Engineering report and inventory record — confirm the structure’s condition rating and that the proposed work addresses it.
  • Letters of support — optional but read. Letters from the communities on both sides of the crossing carry the most weight.
  • Attachments are kept for the life of the award plus three years, then destroyed under the department’s records schedule.

Why we ask for this, and how it is used
  • Submitting locks the application for review. You can withdraw it from your dashboard at any time before the review begins.
  • A confirmation number is issued immediately and emailed to the account that submitted.
  • Decisions are expected within 120 days of the application deadline. Every applicant is notified either way.
